title: Controlling Severe Bleeding
summary: How to stop life-threatening blood loss using direct pressure and tourniquets.
contentMarkdown:
## Controlling Severe Bleeding

### Step 1 — Call for Help
If possible, call emergency services **before** starting treatment.

### Step 2 — Apply Direct Pressure
- Use a clean cloth, bandage, or any available fabric.
- Press **firmly** on the wound — do not lift to check.
- Maintain pressure for at least **10 minutes**.

### Step 3 — Tourniquet (Limb Only)
If bleeding does not stop and the wound is on an arm or leg:
1. Apply tourniquet **5–7 cm above** the wound (not on a joint).
2. Tighten until bleeding stops.
3. **Write the time applied** on the skin with a pen.
4. Never remove a tourniquet in the field.

### Step 4 — Keep the Person Calm
- Lay the person down.
- Elevate the injured limb if no fracture is suspected.
- Keep them warm to prevent shock.

> **Warning**: Do not remove embedded objects. Pack gauze around them.

### Signs of Shock to Watch For
- Pale, cold, or clammy skin
- Rapid, weak pulse
- Confusion or loss of consciousness

title: Treating Burns
summary: Immediate actions for minor and major burn injuries.
contentMarkdown:
## Treating Burns

### Classify the Burn
| Degree | Appearance | Action |
|--------|------------|--------|
| 1st | Red, no blisters | Cool water, no creams |
| 2nd | Blisters, swelling | Cool water, loose dressing |
| 3rd | White/charred | Seek immediate care |

### For Minor Burns (1st & 2nd Degree)
1. **Cool** the burn under clean running water for **10–20 minutes**.
2. **Do NOT** use ice, butter, toothpaste, or oils.
3. Cover loosely with a **non-fluffy sterile dressing**.
4. Take a pain reliever if available.

### For Major Burns (3rd Degree / Large Area)
- Do **not** remove burned clothing stuck to skin.
- Cover with a clean, moist cloth.
- Treat for shock (keep warm, lay down, raise legs).
- Get to medical care as fast as possible.

### What to Avoid
- Breaking blisters
- Applying any household remedies
- Tight bandages

title: Shelter-In-Place Protocol
summary: How to safely shelter inside a building during an attack or chemical hazard.
contentMarkdown:
## Shelter-In-Place Protocol

### When to Shelter In Place
- Active artillery or air strike nearby
- Chemical or biological hazard outside
- Authorities issue a shelter-in-place order

### Choose Your Room
- An **interior room** above ground level (not basement if flooding risk).
- Fewest windows and doors.
- Ideally above the flood plain.

### Seal the Room
1. Close all windows and doors.
2. Use **duct tape and plastic sheeting** to seal gaps around doors, windows, and vents.
3. Seal fireplace dampers and exhaust fans.

### Supplies to Have Ready
- Water (at least 4 litres per person per day)
- Food for 72 hours
- Battery-powered or hand-crank radio
- First aid kit
- Flashlight with extra batteries
- Medications

### While Sheltered
- Keep a battery-powered radio tuned to emergency broadcasts.
- Check on other household members regularly.
- Limit phone use to preserve battery.

### When to Leave
- Follow official instructions only.
- Ventilate the room for a few minutes before leaving if a chemical event is suspected.

title: 72-Hour Go-Bag Checklist
summary: Everything you need in a bug-out bag to survive 72 hours on the move.
contentMarkdown:
## 72-Hour Go-Bag Checklist

Pack your bag in advance. Refresh water and food every 6 months.

### Water & Food
- [ ] 2 litres of water per person
- [ ] Water purification tablets
- [ ] High-energy non-perishable food (energy bars, canned goods)
- [ ] Manual can opener

### Documents & Money
- [ ] Photocopies of ID, passport, insurance cards
- [ ] Small amount of cash (cards may not work)
- [ ] USB drive with digital copies of documents

### First Aid
- [ ] Pre-stocked first aid kit
- [ ] 7-day supply of prescription medications
- [ ] Glasses / contact lenses + solution

### Tools & Safety
- [ ] Flashlight + extra batteries
- [ ] Multi-tool or pocket knife
- [ ] Whistle (signal for help)
- [ ] Dust masks (N95 or better)
- [ ] Waterproof matches or lighter
- [ ] Emergency blanket (Mylar)

### Communication
- [ ] Battery-powered or hand-crank radio
- [ ] Fully charged mobile phone + portable charger
- [ ] Written list of key phone numbers

### Clothing
- [ ] One change of clothes per person
- [ ] Sturdy, closed-toe shoes
- [ ] Rain poncho

### Special Needs
- [ ] Infant formula / diapers (if needed)
- [ ] Pet food (if applicable)
- [ ] Comfort item for children

title: Emergency Water Purification
summary: Safe methods to make water drinkable without electricity or specialty equipment.
contentMarkdown:
## Emergency Water Purification

> **Rule**: When in doubt, purify it.

### Method 1 — Boiling (Most Reliable)
1. Bring water to a **rolling boil** for at least **1 minute**.
2. At altitudes above 2,000 m: boil for **3 minutes**.
3. Let cool and store in a clean covered container.

### Method 2 — Chemical Disinfection
**Unscented household bleach (5–8% chlorine)**:
- Clear water: **8 drops per litre**
- Cloudy water: **16 drops per litre**
- Stir, wait **30 minutes** before drinking.

**Water purification tablets**:
- Follow manufacturer's instructions.
- Usually 1 tablet per litre; wait 30 minutes.

### Method 3 — Solar Disinfection (SODIS)
1. Fill a clear PET plastic bottle with filtered water.
2. Place in direct sunlight for **6 hours** (or 2 days if cloudy).
3. Effective against bacteria and viruses.

### Pre-treating Cloudy Water
- Filter through a cloth, coffee filter, or sand/gravel layers first.
- This removes sediment and improves disinfection effectiveness.

### Storage
- Use clean, covered containers.
- Do not touch the inside of the container.
- Store away from sunlight and heat.

title: CPR — Basic Life Support
summary: Step-by-step hands-only and full CPR for adults.
contentMarkdown:
## CPR — Basic Life Support

### Check Scene Safety First
Do not approach if the area is unsafe (fire, unstable structure, etc.).

### Check the Person
1. Tap the shoulder firmly: **"Are you okay?"**
2. If no response → Call emergency services immediately.

### Hands-Only CPR (Untrained)
1. Place heel of one hand on the **centre of the chest**.
2. Place other hand on top, interlace fingers.
3. Push **hard and fast** — at least **5 cm deep** at **100–120 beats/minute** (roughly the beat of *Stayin' Alive*).
4. Do not stop until help arrives or the person recovers.

### Full CPR (Trained)
- **30 chest compressions** → **2 rescue breaths**
- Tilt head back, lift chin, pinch nose, seal mouth, breathe for 1 second.
- Repeat cycle.

### Using an AED (If Available)
1. Turn on the AED and follow voice prompts.
2. Attach pads as shown on the diagrams.
3. Clear everyone → press shock button if advised.
4. Resume CPR immediately after shock.

### For Children (1–8 years)
- Use **one or two hands** depending on child's size.
- Compress **4 cm deep**.
- Use gentle rescue breaths.

### Stop CPR If
- Scene becomes unsafe
- Person shows clear signs of life
- AED is ready to analyse
- Professional responders take over
